onThisDay.fact: As of January 1, 2026, the Florida Forest Service reported that drought and wildfire conditions were beginning to escalate across North Florida — a situation that would intensify throughout the month.
Columbia County commissioners held an emergency meeting to approve a county-wide burn ban at the request of the Florida Forest Service, amid the worst drought conditions in 25 years.

The Battle of Olustee was fought near present-day Olustee, east of Lake City on US-90 — the largest Civil War engagement in Florida. Nearly 10,000 troops clashed, including three U.S. Colored Regiments. The 54th Massachusetts, later immortalized in the film 'Glory,' fought at Olustee.
onThisDay.source: National Park Service / Florida State Parks

onThisDay.fact: The railroad arrived in Fort White in 1888, sparking a boom in phosphate mining, turpentine production, and agriculture that grew the town's population to nearly 2,000. Fort White briefly became the second largest city in Columbia County.

The original Fort White military fort, built in 1836 during the Second Seminole War to protect the Cow Creek settlement, was abandoned on this day due to illness among the troops. No remains of the fort are visible today.
onThisDay.source: Town of Fort White Official History

onThisDay.fact: The Town of Fort White was officially incorporated as a municipality in 1884, named after the military fort that had been built nearby nearly 50 years earlier during the Second Seminole War.

Fort White was constructed as a military fort during the Second Seminole War in 1836 to protect the Cow Creek settlement. Supplies were brought up the Santa Fe River by steamboat and distributed to other nearby forts and settlers.
onThisDay.source: Town of Fort White Official History

onThisDay.fact: By 1910, Fort White's largest phosphate deposits were depleted and mining ceased. The boll weevil later ended cotton farming before World War I, shrinking the population from nearly 2,000 to just a few hundred — mostly ranchers, farmers, and foresters.
onThisDay.source: Town of Fort White Official History

onThisDay.fact: The State of Florida purchased 2,241 acres of Ichetucknee spring and river property from the Loncala Phosphate Corporation in 1970. The property became Ichetucknee Springs State Park, transforming the area's identity and economy.

The head spring of the Ichetucknee River was declared a National Natural Landmark by the U.S. Department of the Interior in 1972. The spring pumps 233 million gallons of crystal-clear water daily at a constant 72°F.

Fort White High School was built in 1915. The auditorium was added in 1936, and the last graduating class from the original school was in 1969. The historic school building is now part of the Fort White Public School Historic District.

Severe freezes in the winters of 1896 and 1897 destroyed Fort White's citrus industry, ending the boom that had made the town the second largest city in Columbia County. The population never fully recovered.

The area of the original Fort White military fort, 4 miles west of town on the Santa Fe River, became the Fort White Wildlife and Environmental Area in 1997 — preserving the site where the town's story began.

During the Second Seminole War, Seminole leader Halpatter Tustenuggee (Alligator Warrior), chief of what is now Lake City (then called 'Alligator Town'), led resistance in the region around Fort White. He is buried at Tustenuggee Methodist Cemetery near Fort White.
Fort White was officially founded in 1870 as a settlement, moving 4 miles east from the original fort site on the Santa Fe River due to flooding and the anticipated arrival of the railroad.
